compiled_state.description:
# `sign-review` aborts on stray UNTRACKED tracker files — a missed site of already-fixed bug d7cb

## Symptom

`rebar review-plan <id>` returns **PASS** but cannot sign, and the documented recovery
`rebar sign-review <id>` fails **deterministically** (3/3, not contention):

```
{"ok": false, "signed": false, "verdict": "PASS",
 "reason": "plan review generation could not be collected: store-read-failure"}
```

Net effect: a plan that PASSED cannot be signed, so `claim` and the plan-review CLOSE gate stay
blocked on a clean PASS. The billable LLM review runs and passes, and only then can the result not
be persisted — the work is paid for and discarded.

## CORRECTION to this ticket's original filing

This ticket originally named `attest.py:406` as the cause. That was a **lead, and it is refuted**
as the source of this symptom: the message text is emitted only at `resign.py:153`, wrapping
`generation.collect`, and `attest.py` is not on that path. `attest.py` is a *sibling* (below), not
the cause.

## PROVEN root cause

`src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py:146` calls

```python
initial_generation = generation.collect(ticket_id, repo_root=repo_root)
```

omitting `ignore_untracked`, which defaults to `False`
(`generation.collect(..., ignore_untracked: bool = False)`). That reaches
`collect_plan_relation_snapshot(ignore_untracked=False)` → `tracker_head_sha(tracker)` strict, which runs

```python
("status", "--porcelain")            # untracked INCLUDED
```

instead of `("status","--porcelain","--untracked-files=no")`. Any untracked file makes the output
non-empty → `_store_error` → `store-read-failure` → resign's wrapper reports
"plan review generation could not be collected".

## Experimental proof (runtime, isolated temp git repo)

| condition | strict (`ignore_untracked=False`) | lenient (`True`) |
|---|---|---|
| clean tree | OK (control) | OK |
| untracked `.tmp-event-*` (partial JSON) | **RAISE store-read-failure** | OK |
| untracked file, UNRELATED name + content | **RAISE store-read-failure** | OK |
| TRACKED dirty (modified file) | RAISE | **RAISE** |

Row 3 **refutes** the competing "partial-JSON parse failure" hypothesis: the failure is entirely
content- and name-agnostic, purely the `git status` check. Row 4 shows the flag does NOT weaken the
real guarantee — tracked dirty state still fails, as it must.

Field observation that opened the case: two orphaned `.tmp-event-*` files (~16h stale, 0 tracked-dirty
/ 2 untracked) in the shared tracker; moving them out made the identical `sign-review` succeed with
nothing else changed.

## Why it is a DEFECT (cited authority, not the reporter's expectation)

This is a **missed site of an already-fixed bug class**. Bug `d7cb-22ae` (commit `1475e2868`,
"d7cb: plan-review tolerates unrelated untracked shared-tracker files") fixed exactly this in two
places and landed two regression tests that state the contract:

- `tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py::test_review_plan_preflight_tolerates_unrelated_untracked_tracker_files`
- `tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py::test_sign_manifest_fence_tolerates_unrelated_untracked_tracker_files`
  — labelled "**sibling on the SIGNING path**", and stating that otherwise a stray artifact
  "aborts signing (`store-read-failure`), so no durable attestation is persisted and the plan-review
  claim gate cannot pass even for a clean plan".

That fix touched `__init__.py` and `generation.py` but **never `resign.py`**. The intended behaviour
is therefore already established and this site violates it.

## Blast radius

`.tickets-tracker` is symlinked into every session, so ONE crashed writer anywhere blocks signing for
every concurrent session on the machine — the same machine-wide collapse d7cb was raised to prevent.

## SIBLINGS found by sweeping every untracked-sensitive call site

| site | call | symptom when an untracked file exists |
|---|---|---|
| `resign.py:146` | `generation.collect(...)` | HARD FAIL — `sign-review` refuses (this ticket's confirmed cause) |
| `orchestrator.py:650` | `generation.collect(...)` | SILENT COST — wrapped in `except Exception: return None` ("unstable generation falls back to a full review"), so a stray file forces a full multi-pass LLM re-review instead of the cheap drift-refresh probe |
| `attest.py:139` | `collect_plan_relation_snapshot(...)` | aborts signing on the fallback path (when no `initial_generation`/snapshot is supplied) |
| `attest.py:406` | `collect_plan_relation_snapshot(...)` | same, in `refresh_attestation` |

Already correct (fixed by d7cb): `__init__.py:495`, `generation.py:131/133/173`.

`orchestrator.py:650` is the most insidious: it fails INVISIBLY and the only symptom is money and
latency — a full LLM review where a cheap probe was intended.

## Approach

Pass `ignore_untracked=True` at each of the four sites. These are all READS that fingerprint the
COMMITTED head, which untracked files cannot change; the authoritative under-lock re-check
(`generation.py:173`) already tolerates them, so this makes the class consistent.

## Scope

- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/resign.py` — the confirmed defect.
- `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/orchestrator.py`, `src/rebar/llm/plan_review/attest.py` — siblings.
- `tests/unit/test_plan_relation_snapshot.py` — regression tests beside the two existing d7cb siblings.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] a test asserts `resign_plan_review` still signs a valid PASS when an UNRELATED untracked file
      exists in the tracker, and fails RED before the fix
- [ ] a test asserts TRACKED dirty state still blocks these paths — the flag must not weaken the
      real guarantee
- [ ] the orchestrator drift-refresh path does not silently fall back to a full review because of an
      untracked file
- [ ] every `collect_plan_relation_snapshot` / `generation.collect` call site in `src/rebar` either
      passes `ignore_untracked=True` or carries a comment saying why strictness is intended
compiled_state.title: sign-review fails on stray untracked tracker files: attest.py omits ignore_untracked
